# Support Vector Machines and Kernel Methods

## Learning Objectives
- Explain margins and support vectors.
- Describe hard- and soft-margin classification.
- Explain the kernel trick conceptually.
- Tune SVM hyperparameters using validation.
- Recognize when feature scaling is essential.

## Why This Matters
Support vector machines illustrate how geometry, optimization, and nonlinear feature spaces combine to produce powerful predictive models.

## Real-World Problem
Can a nonlinear boundary separate complex patient or student profiles better than a linear classifier?

## Common Mistakes
- Failing to scale features.
- Tuning on the test set.
- Using complex kernels without justification.
- Treating SVM scores as calibrated probabilities.

## Professor's Challenge

## Research Extension
Study performance, calibration, and computational tradeoffs across kernels.

## Reproducibility Check

## Key Takeaways
- SVMs connect geometry and optimization.
- Kernel methods enable nonlinear decision boundaries.
- Proper scaling and validation are essential.
